title: Proactive KV Segment Reassignment & Fragmentation-Mitigation Playbook
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Problem: Ongoing KV cache fragmentation on high-concurrency workloads leads to increased allocation latency, degraded continuous-batching efficiency (reduced contiguous spans), and occasional OOM/host-spill events under transient hotspots. Existing background compaction is heavy-handed and causes move-amplification spikes during P95 token tails.

Goal: Introduce a "proactive segment reassignment" strategy combined with a lightweight "slab-taper" allocation profile and gap-aware micro-grooms to reduce fragmentation without large synchronous compaction pauses. The approach must integrate with continuous batching so batch-affine requests get contiguous KV spans to improve kernel locality and reduce per-token latency.

Summary of the approach:
- Track segment-level hotness and scatter metrics (compactness, gap-ratio, allocation churn).
- When a segment's gap-ratio crosses the scatter threshold and heat is low, schedule an epoched, lockless reassignment that moves only live spans (copy-on-write) into tapered slabs sized for expected span lengths.
- Use a small, per-GPU "churn buffer" (in GPU memory) for short-lived spans to avoid polluting long-lived slabs. Periodically flush the churn buffer into appropriately sized slabs during low-util windows.
- Preserve contiguous KV ranges for active batching by preferring allocations that maintain span locality for tokens likely to be co-batched. A batch-affinity heuristic biases placement to neighboring slots when allocation request metadata indicates same request/session.
- If GPU memory pressure spikes, fall back to host-spill policy or lightweight eviction tiered by hotness and latency sensitivity.

Why this is different: Favors incremental, hotness-aware reassignment and allocation shaping (slab-taper + churn buffer) over full compaction; minimizes move amplification and tail latency impact while improving continuous-batching locality.
acceptance_criteria: KV fragmentation ratio (empty slots / total slots) reduced by >= 40% on target workloads vs baseline within 2 hours of warmup
Average allocation latency under burst traffic decreases by >= 15% in our perf harness with continuous batching enabled
P95 token latency for small (< 256 tokens) chat sessions improves or is not regressed more than 5%
Move-amplification (bytes moved per reclaimed byte) stays below 3x on representative RL workload
No increase in OOM incidents in canary fleet; host-spill events are within current baseline range
Telemetry for segment reassignment operations available in Console (events, durations, bytes moved, triggering heuristics)
design_decisions: Use per-GPU epoched moves with sequence numbers to avoid global locks; moves are idempotent and can be retried safely
Introduce slab-taper tiers (tiny, small, medium, large) sized by empirical token-span length distributions rather than fixed powers-of-two
Maintain a small GPU-resident churn buffer per serving thread to absorb transient allocations and reduce fragmentation of long-lived slabs
Batch-affinity hints flow from the request router into allocation path (three-bit affinity token) to bias contiguous placement
Defer heavyweight compaction to an offline maintenance window; proactive reassignment handles steady-state fragmentation
tradeoffs: Pros: Lower tail latency impact due to incremental moves; better batch locality; reduced synchronous compaction
Cons: Additional metadata (hotness counters, gap-ratio) increases memory overhead by ~1-2% and some CPU scheduling complexity
Pros: Churn buffer improves short-lived allocation speed; reduces cross-slab fragmentation
Cons: Churn buffer flushes may temporarily increase memcpy load on GPU if not rate limited
Requires careful tuning of scatter thresholds to avoid repeated oscillation (migrating the same spans back and forth)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 2w): implement hotness/gap tracking probe and slack-safe epoched move primitives in the allocator runtime; add debug-only telemetry hooks
Phase 2 (prototype, 3w): implement slab-taper placement policy + churn buffer; add affinity hint plumbing through router and request context
Phase 3 (perf-testing, 2w): run synthetic and replay workloads comparing fragmentation, allocation latency, and batching locality; tune taper sizes and scatter thresholds
Phase 4 (canary, 2w): deploy to 5% of serving fleet with aggressive telemetry and automatic rollback on defined signals
Phase 5 (rollout, 2-4w): gradual ramp to 50% then 100%, monitor regressions, iterate on thresholds and telemetry aggregation
telemetry_plan: New metrics: segment_gap_ratio, segment_hotness_score, churn_buffer_utilization, bytes_moved_per_reassignment, reassignment_duration_ms
Tag metrics by model, instance-type, and route to diagnose workload-specific behavior
Expose histograms for allocation_latency and per-request KV hit-rate; correlate with batch_size buckets
Add Console dashboard: Fragmentation Overview (global + per-region), Reassignment Events timeline, Move Amplification graph
Create alert rules: rapid increase in reassignment_rate OR bytes_moved > X within 5m triggers paged alert; P95 allocation_latency > threshold triggers warning
test_plan: Unit tests: epoched move primitives, idempotent replay under simulated races
Integration tests: churn buffer correctness, affinity hint correctness across router/allocator boundary
Perf harness: replay production trace for 7 days worth of requests at 2x QPS; measure fragmentation and batch locality
Chaos test: force GPU memory pressure and validate fallback to host-spill and safe evictions
Canary validation suite: smoke checks + telemetry assertions (no OOMs, reassignment rate within expected band)
rollout_plan: Start with internal perf cluster: enable feature-flagged path and run overnight replay tests
Canary at 5%: monitor fragmentation metrics and tail latency for 48h
If stable, ramp to 25% for 72h with stake holders notified (SRE, Product, Console team)
Post-ramp review: collect telemetry, adjust thresholds; schedule maintenance window for offline compaction tuning if needed
Full rollout with automated throttling based on alert signals and rollback to previous allocator release on high-severity regressions
